details.label: Discussion
details.text: A thermal-induced surface low has materialized across central KS, resulting in the development of an effective dryline extending from roughly Rice to Butler Counties, and a weak cold front drifting southward roughly from Rush County and points west. Near the low and between these two boundaries, maximized convergence has resulted in an agitated CU field, with attempts at convective initiation noted. Thunderstorm development and maintenance is very uncertain in this scenario, with conditions both favorable and hostile convection noted. Deep-layer ascent is quite weak across central KS, with the 22Z mesoanalysis showing appreciable MLCINH in place, but the combination of strong heating and low-level convergence may compensate to support supercell development given the presence of 3000+ J/kg MLCAPE amid 50-60 kts of effective bulk shear. If supercells develop and sustain themselves, severe wind and hail may occur, and an instance of 2+ inch diameter hail cannot be ruled out. Convective trends will continue to be closely monitored for successful attempts at convective initiation

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Thunderstorms across southern Wisconsin have taken on a more linear/bowing mode over the last hour. The line has produced a few instances of damaging wind, with measured gusts up to 61 mph. Deep layer flow is largely westerly, which will likely push the line eastward across southern Wisconsin through the evening with damaging wind becoming the main threat. Watch issuance further south of WW595 remains uncertain. Deep layer flow decreases further south, with mid-level cloud cover in place and less instability. Additionally, lapse rate profiles are meager. A couple of cells have developed further west across far eastern Iowa. These may pose some potential for large hail in the short term. It remains uncertain that coverage/duration will warrant additional watch issuance at this time but this area will be monitored

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Thunderstorm activity is shifting eastward across Lake Michigan this evening. Downstream, the air mass is only marginally unstable, with MLCAPE around 250-500 J/kg. Deep layer flow is seasonably strong, with deep layer shear 35-45 kts across the northern lower Michigan Peninsula. RAOB profiles from APX (Gaylord, MI) shows a long straight hodograph, which would be supportive of splitting supercells capable of large hail and damaging wind. Damaging wind potential may be further supported by steep low level lapse rates (around 8 C/km). There remains some uncertainty with how long supercells will be sustained, given the only marginally favorable thermodynamics. This area will be monitored for watch potential
